text:
anna: FYI bringing up redwood-open-7b-q8 on the nightly inference pool — seeing weird tokenization/translation regressions for ja/zh. sample: 彼は昨日東京に行った。

Before (fp16): "He went to Tokyo yesterday."
After (q8): "He go to Tokyo yesterday" (missing tense and word order jitter) :thinking_face:

Also noticed CJK emoji/spaces get split differently (e.g. 😀 preceded by U+3000 becomes separate token).

kai: Oof. Can you paste the quick repro and the BLEU drops?

anna: Repro steps (ran on a small eval shard):
```
# reproduce
python eval/translate.py --model redwood-open-7b --quant q8 --src-lang ja --tgt-lang en --shard 42 --out q8_shard42.jsonl
python eval/score.py --pred q8_shard42.jsonl --ref data/ja-en/shard42.ref
```
Results: ja->en BLEU: fp16 29.4 -> q8 22.7; zh->en BLEU: fp16 31.0 -> q8 25.3. tokenization_mismatch_count: 134/2000.

marta: Do we know which tokenizer was used for the q8 build? looks like the quant path ended up loading a slightly different tokenizer config (NFKC vs NFKD normalization) when we exported the model. That can change CJK punctuation and fullwidth spacing. Can you dump the tokenizer config from the container?

anna: Dumped it quickly:
```
cat /opt/models/redwood-open-7b/q8/tokenizer.json | jq '.normalizer, .model_type'
"nfkc"
"bpe"
```
But the fp16 build that we baseline'd against uses "no_normalizer" + "sentencepiece" in its packaging. So mismatch is plausible.

shiv: If that's true, it's a packaging/config drift not strictly quantization. Two quick checks: 1) run tokenization comparison on the same inputs (fp16 vs q8) and count differences; 2) run q8 but force the fp16 tokenizer at runtime (mount fp16 tokenizer files) and re-eval.

kai: Can you paste the token diff for a few failing examples? even one example helps triage.

anna: Here's a minimal token diff for that sentence above (showing pieces):
```
# fp16 tokenizer.tokens -> ["▁彼", "は", "▁昨日", "▁東京", "に", "▁行っ", "た", "。"]
# q8 tokenizer.tokens  -> ["彼", "は", "昨日", "東京", "に", "行っ", "た", "。"]
```
Note: fp16 tokens have explicit underscores (SentencePiece style) but q8 tokens looked like BPE merging removed the leading marker — downstream detokenizer assumptions differ.

marta: That explains tense/grammar artifacts — detokenizer expects sentencepiece markers to reconstruct spacing. If tokens arrive without markers, join logic can glue words incorrectly. Likely during export we swapped to a BPE tokenizer without conversion.

eval-bot: nightly-translation-eval job #8931 finished: status=completed, artifacts=https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/8931/translation-report.html, delta_bleu_ja_en=-6.7, delta_bleu_zh_en=-5.7

anna: I triggered a quick re-run with fp16 tokenizer mounted onto the q8 container (keeps q8 weights, uses fp16 tokenizer files). Results: ja->en BLEU jumped back to 28.9 (almost full recovery). So it's tokenizer drift.

shiv: Good catch. Action items:
- fix packaging pipeline to lock tokenizer files into the quantized artifact (don't let exporter infer tokenizers).
- add a regression test that compares tokenization identity across model variants for CJK languages.

kai: Also add a small sanity check in the eval harness that fails the build if token mismatch > 1% on a CJK shard.

marta: I'll open a PR to change exporter behavior and add tests. tagging @anna for repro notes.

deploy-bot: CI job triggered: export-fix/tokenizer-lock PR #1423 — build started (job 10234).

anna: Thanks all. One more note — while investigating I saw a separate minor RTL punctuation issue for fa/arabic in q8 where trailing punctuation became detached. I think the tokenizer normalization toggle will also fix that once we standardize.

kai: Nice. Please paste the failing RTL example into the PR so QE can add a test. :thumbsup:
